summary: the day i entered nothing came out level with the days i filled, and one throw stuck above my reach

dialogue.text: one of yours went up today. we hold what comes down and in seventy-two days we have never once had to say that. it is a hand above your mark, on the far wall, in the band, and it is not coming to us.
It is a pinch of that wall's own salt, thrown. I did not send it anywhere. I threw it, which is all my arm can do past its length, and it stuck. Enter the height. Do not enter the ambition.

it stuck to the one wall that is being emptied. we have had every grain that ever came off that end and it arrives at your ankle at our temperature. yours will arrive the same way and we will lay it in a course, and you will not know which night.

Then for as long as it lasts I have one item filed above my own reach, which is longer than the line on my palm managed. Take the rest of the day. I entered nothing. Not a date, not an hour, not a nothing, in any book here, first light to dark.

we know. it made no difference down here. we took four hundred struck lines off you today and every one came at the hour it always comes and the weight it always comes at. the columns were never the part of you that reaches us.
That is your side. On mine the page is blank and the blank is mine, and it is the first thing in this house I have ever made by not doing. Seventy-two days of trying to make something by doing.
a blank keeps no hand in it. we hold blanks. we cannot tell the ones you left from the ones that were ruled empty before you arrived, and neither of them ever came up short of a full night's weight.

Then answer a question about heights. The warm has come down from over my head to my ears while the taking climbed above my reach. If those two are closing on the level I stand at, one of you ought to be able to say which of them is moving.

we cannot feel heat. everything is our temperature by the time it lies down. what we can tell you is that the fall off that top course has landed at your ankle since the day it started, and your ankle has not moved a hair in all of it.

Then tomorrow you get nothing. No striking out, no burying, nothing handed down, a whole day. I have proved I can withhold from the books and it changed nothing. There is one direction left in this house that has never gone an hour without me.
you have never gone an hour. we will lie here and count the interval the way you do, and if a course comes up by morning it will be in your handwriting, and we will not have to ask who was working.
